events.title: Birth of Nicolaus Copernicus
events.description: Nicolaus Copernicus was born in Toruń, Poland. He became a mathematician and astronomer who formulated a heliocentric model of the universe, placing the Sun rather than the Earth at its center.
events.significance: His work, published in De revolutionibus orbium coelestium in 1543, launched the Copernican Revolution and was a foundational moment in the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Edison Patents the Phonograph
events.description: Thomas Edison was granted U.S. Patent No. 200,521 for the phonograph, a device capable of recording and reproducing sound.
events.significance: The phonograph was the first device to record and play back sound, laying the groundwork for the recorded music industry and modern audio technology.

events.title: Executive Order 9066 Signed
events.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066, authorizing the forced removal of people from designated military zones during World War II. It was used to intern roughly 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them U.S. citizens.
events.significance: The order became one of the most notorious civil liberties violations in American history, and the U.S. government formally apologized and offered reparations in the Civil Liberties Act of 1988.

events.title: Bombing of Darwin
events.description: Japanese aircraft launched the first and largest single attack by a foreign power on Australia, striking the northern city of Darwin and ships in its harbor. More than 230 people were killed.
events.significance: The raid brought World War II directly to Australian soil and heightened fears of a Japanese invasion, shaping Australia's wartime strategy and its alliance with the United States.

events.title: Battle of Iwo Jima Begins
events.description: U.S. Marines landed on the island of Iwo Jima in the Pacific, beginning one of the bloodiest battles of World War II against entrenched Japanese defenders.
events.significance: The month-long battle gave the U.S. an important position for air operations against Japan and produced the iconic flag-raising photograph on Mount Suribachi.
